title: How OpenTakeoff works
description: A takeoff canvas that runs entirely in your browser — no account, no upload, no install. Open a plan, set the scale, measure the finishes, export a priced quantity report.
footer_intro: This is the short version. The full manual covers conditions, markups and RFIs, revisions, the report and exports, the Agent panel, and driving OpenTakeoff from an AI agent over MCP —
start.open_plan_desc: Drag a PDF, an image, or a whole .zip plan set onto the canvas — or click Load sample plan to use the bundled VA finish plan. Nothing leaves your machine.
start.set_scale_desc: Every quantity depends on it. The Scale menu offers what the sheet's own title block states; hover it to preview a calibrated ruler on the drawing, or calibrate two points of a known dimension. Remembered per sheet.
start.add_condition_desc: A condition is a finish — CPT-1, LVT, base. Give it a tag, a waste %, and a colour. Press 1–9 to arm one.
start.measure_desc: One-Click a room and it selects itself; or trace by hand with Area, Rectangle, Linear or Count. In One-Click, ⏎ creates it.
start.read_report_desc: REPORT totals every condition, applies waste, and gives you order quantities, a buy list, and CSV / Excel export.
tools.oneclick: One-Click Area — click inside a room, it selects itself
tools.calibrate: Check a dimension against what the drawing says
tools.dictation: Push-to-talk dictation — release runs it, Esc discards
draw.finish: Finish the shape. In One-Click: Create the selection
draw.backspace: Back out one step — the last point, then the picked vertex, the region, the selected shape, the markup
draw.undo: Mid-trace pops the last point; otherwise undo
draw.escape: Back out one level — vertex pick first, then anything in progress
draw.shift_hold: Force the 45° angle lock at any cursor angle
draw.option_click: In One-Click: carve a cutout inside a selected space
draw.shift_click: Insert a vertex at an edge midpoint, and drag it
view.space_hold: Pan with any tool armed — as does middle-drag or right-drag
view.focus: Focus mode — collapse the chrome, trade it for canvas height
